title: Evaluating the Impact of Temperature on Agent Safety Behavior and Monitor Detectability

original_idea.body:
# Evaluating the Impact of Temperature on Agent Safety Behavior and Monitor Detectability

**Problem:** LLM sampling temperature affects output diversity and unpredictability. Higher temperature may produce more unpredictable safety-relevant behaviors that are also harder for monitors to classify.

**Direction:** Run agents at temperature settings from 0.0 to 1.5. Measure safety violation rates and monitoring detection rates at each temperature. Characterize the temperature-safety and temperature-detectability relationships.

**Why it matters:** Temperature is a deployment hyperparameter with direct safety implications. Understanding its effects on both safety violations and monitoring reliability informs safe deployment configurations.

**Relevant context:** LLM temperature and safety behavior; monitoring accuracy; agent deployment.
